2609.14467.title: Bridging the Modality Gap in Long-Form Clinical Audio: A Comparative Study of Lightweight and Heavyweight End-to-End SOAP Generation
2609.14467.paper_summary: Automating clinical documentation from long-form doctor-patient conversations remains challenging for modern audio-language models. While cascaded ASR systems perform well, end-to-end (E2E) models often struggle with information loss and hallucinations on extended audio. For the BeTraC 2026 challenge, the ASLP team presents a fully E2E multimodal system that generates structured SOAP notes directly from audio, bypassing intermediate transcripts. We constructed a 1.41-million-sample multi-task corpus and applied a multi-stage pipeline: domain pre-training, supervised fine-tuning, and reward optimization. Evaluating the architecture under both Lightweight (3B) and Heavyweight (30B) constraints reveals that each training stage progressively enhances performance. Furthermore, scaling to 30B parameters substantially boosts concept extraction and summarization quality. Ultimately, our E2E systems consistently outperform representative cascaded ASR+LLM baselines, proving the efficacy of direct multimodal optimization for clinical documentation.
2609.14467.paper_summary_zh: 自動化長篇醫生-病人對話的臨床文檔對於現代音頻語言模型來說仍然具有挑戰性。雖然級聯自動語音識別（ASR）系統表現良好，但端到端（E2E）模型在處理延長音頻時常常面臨信息損失和幻覺的問題。針對 BeTraC 2026 挑戰，ASLP 團隊提出了一個完全的 E2E 多模態系統，該系統直接從音頻生成結構化的 SOAP 記錄，跳過中間的轉錄。我們構建了一個包含 141 萬樣本的多任務語料庫，並應用了一個多階段流程：領域預訓練、監督微調和獎勵優化。在輕量級（3B）和重型（30B）約束下評估架構顯示，每個訓練階段都逐步提高了性能。此外，擴展到 30B 參數顯著提升了概念提取和總結質量。最終，我們的 E2E 系統始終超越了代表性的級聯 ASR+LLM 基準，證明了直接多模態優化在臨床文檔中的有效性。
